text:
alex: quick follow-up to the RFC: we need to hammer down how priority TTLs behave across the ingestion pipeline. i sketched a concrete enforcement model below.

maria: nice, short on time today but skimmed. question: is priority a binary flag or multi-level (p0/p1/etc)?

alex: multi-level (p0/p1/p2) but TTL semantics the same. higher priority consumes tokens faster.

cheng: cost guardrails: i'd rather we think in tokens-per-second and a hard global cap per tenant. otherwise a single bad client can burn us.
sam: agree. practical defaults: per-tenant refill rate (tokens/sec), bucket size, and default token cost per priority (p0=10, p1=3, p2=1).

taylor: where do we check tokens? doing checks at the edge is fastest for routing, but incurs cross-region consistency issues.

jen: operationally we can do a two-step check: 1) fast local check at edge (best-effort) 2) authoritative check at central ingress that can downgrade retroactively and emit audit. avoids route stalls.

cheng: if central downgrades after routing happened, we must annotate envelopes with "priority_reconciled=true" and reason. compactor needs to respect the authoritative flag.

alex: also propose that TTL be stored as expiry_ts (unix epoch) in envelope header to avoid delta math. header names: x-rt-priority, x-rt-requested-priority, x-rt-expiry-ts.
maria: can we include original_requested_priority too so analytics can see intent vs actual?

alex: yes store both requested and effective priority. and include a "priority_downgraded_reason" tag when downgraded.

sam: tests: need matrix for combinations (edge accept + central downgrade, late enrichment after expiry, compactor sees expired vs not).

ingest-bot: ci-note: unit tests added for expiry_ts parsing + token-bucket edge vs central (PR 7902). :white_check_mark:

jen: compactor contract: compactor must preserve the envelope header until either expiry_ts passes AND the envelope is eligible for normal sampling/eviction, OR there is an authoritative downgrade marker. basically: do not evict based solely on local timestamps unless headers indicate allowed.

cheng: concrete: compactor keeps priority headers until it sees either (a) expiry_ts < now and no reclassify request OR (b) a "priority_revoked=true" envelope flag from central. that ensures chargeback/retention accounting stays correct.

taylor: storage impact: keeping headers in compaction index increases index size. we should only materialize minimal fields: expiry_ts, effective_priority, original_priority, downgrade_reason. all as short ints/enums.
maria: console needs to show remaining tokens, burn rate, and a headline "priority budget at X%" with links to scoped queries. ops needs emergency toggle per-tenant.

alex: policy proposal: default high_priority_ttl = 30s, default bucket refill = 1 token/sec, token cost p0=10, p1=3, p2=1, tenant max-ttl = 24h only for enterprise with opt-in. product/legal to confirm.

cheng: GDPR/legal guardrails: priorities must not permit retention below legal minima. i.e., you can't priority-away data deletion. priority only upgrades retention short-term, not override legal retention config.
sam: also ensure audit trail includes who requested priority when issued by server-side code (service principal) vs client. need to tie to api_key/identity.

jen: implementation notes: ingest-controller will run token-bucket checks and emit a small signed header (sig) so central can verify edge decisions. fallback: for Dedicated, memcached shared bucket; Hosted use centralized redis cluster for low-latency checks.
taylor: perf: edge check should be <1ms p95; central verify budget check in kafka consumer path ok at a few ms.

alex: late enrichment behavior: enrichment can add attributes but cannot increase effective_priority or extend expiry_ts. it can ping a manual reclassify API that starts a human review workflow. reclassify requires audit log and owner approval unless tenant has auto-reclassify flag.

maria: action items: 1) product/legal max-ttl decision (maria) 2) ingest-controller prototype w/ token-bucket + sig header (taylor + cheng) 3) compactor contract doc + minimal field set (jen) 4) Console UX ticket for token visibility & emergency toggle (maria) 5) audit log + reclassify workflow stub (sam).

alex: timeline: prototype this sprint, internal canary next week, GA in 2 sprints assuming no surprises.

cheng: nit: use epoch ms for expiry_ts to handle sub-second TTLs uniformly.

alex: ok epoch ms, add both raw expiry_ms and a human-readable ttl_seconds in debug logs only.

jen: will draft compactor contract + example envelope schema (small JSON blob) and post PR to infra-docs repo.

sam: i'll own the test matrix + e2e scenarios. will add cases for "edge accepted, central revoked", "late enrichment after expiry", and "compactor header persisted vs lost".

maria: thanks team. i'll update product/legal and loop back.

alex: I'll spin up the RFC addendum with header names and minimal enum tables, ping for review.

ingest-bot: deploy-note: ingest-controller prototype deployed to canary cluster (canary-3) at 3887765488. smoke tests running. :rocket:
